hero.headline: Inspiring students to think like engineers.
hero.lead: A coding teacher with a software engineering background. I'm an MoE-registered instructor in Singapore and have taught 130+ students aged 4 to 18. I've helped a student get into their chosen school through DSA, and I've run AI workshops for seniors. I'm studying for a Master in Education (Educational Technology), and I teach in English, Mandarin and Malay.

ooy.title: OOY CIRCLE × DREAMS 2026: Interactive Family-Roots Exhibition Kiosk
ooy.body: I developed a touchscreen kiosk for the exhibition. Visitors find their surname in a database of 20,000+ entries, see their family's migration path from China to Singapore, and build their family tree in English or Chinese. At the end they print a foldable A4 keepsake that combines the tree and the migration route in one card. The system also has a staff admin portal, QR-code links and a print layout at true A4 size. Visitors can scan a QR code to finish their tree at home on their phone and send it back.
ooy.imageCaption: A sample of the printed A4 keepsake. The top half folds over to the back.
ooy.imageAlt: A4 family-roots keepsake generated by the kiosk: migration route on the top half, surname story and family tree on the bottom half

philosophy.label: Teaching philosophy
philosophy.quote: Debugging isn't about mistakes. It's how children learn to stay calm and think logically when something doesn't work the first time.

debug.title: Fix the bug
debug.task: This program should draw a square, but it comes out crooked. Find the problem and fix it.
debug.viewLabel: Switch how the program is shown
debug.status: It turned {n} times, {deg} degrees each, {total} degrees in total.
debug.fixed: Fixed! 4 × 90 = 360 degrees, so it ends up facing the way it started.
hints: Don't change anything yet. Look at the drawing: how is it different from a square?
A square has 4 corners. After the 4 sides, the turtle should be facing the same way it started.
A full turn is 360 degrees. So how many degrees should each turn be?
debug.lesson: This is how I teach debugging: no answers handed over, just questions that lead students to observe, reason, then test their idea.
